# Food Storage Guide / 食材保存指南

> A free bilingual reference for how long food keeps in the pantry, the
> refrigerator and the freezer, and how to store it properly. Traditional
> Chinese (zh-Hant-TW) and English.

Storage timelines are derived from the USDA FSIS FoodKeeper dataset (public
domain, https://catalog.data.gov/dataset/fsis-foodkeeper-data). Food-safety
principles follow published guidance from the USDA, FDA, CDC, WHO, UK FSA,
Taiwan TFDA, Hong Kong CFS, Japan's MAFF and MHLW, Health Canada and Spain's
AESAN. Foods absent from FoodKeeper are researched separately and cite their
sources on the page itself.

## What a timeline means

This distinction is load-bearing and every food page states which applies:

- Refrigerated raw meat, poultry, seafood, dairy, eggs and cooked or prepared
  dishes are SAFETY limits. Discard at the end of the period; the organisms
  involved rarely change how the food looks or smells.
- Freezer timelines are QUALITY only. Food held continuously at -18 C stays
  microbiologically safe indefinitely.
- Pantry timelines are QUALITY.

## Key reference points
- Refrigerator: 4 C (40 F) or below. Taiwan TFDA commonly cites 7 C; Japanese
  food hygiene rules define refrigeration as 10 C or below.
- Freezer: -18 C (0 F).
- Danger zone: 4-60 C (40-140 F). Taiwan TFDA states 7-60 C; Spain's AESAN
  states 5-60 C. These differ because the agencies differ, not because one of
  them is being quoted wrongly.
- Two-hour rule: discard perishable food left in the danger zone for more than
  2 hours, or 1 hour above 32 C (90 F).
- Reheat leftovers to 74 C (165 F).

## Sections
- /zh and /en: home pages with search
- /{locale}/foods: full food index with pantry, fridge and freezer times
- /{locale}/food/{slug}: one food, with storage times, what a timeline means,
  spoilage signs, thawing and FAQ
- /{locale}/category/{category}: one of vegetables, fruits, meat, poultry,
  seafood, dairy-eggs, grains-beans-pasta, baked-goods, baking-staples,
  condiments-sauces, herbs-spices, oils-fats, shelf-stable, snacks-nuts-seeds,
  beverages, frozen-foods, deli-prepared, vegetarian-proteins, baby-food
- /{locale}/guides and /{locale}/guides/{slug}: food-safety guide articles
- /{locale}/methodology: how the data is sourced and what is refused
- /{locale}/corrections: every figure this site declines to copy from its
  source, with the reasoning and the evidence, plus records retired as
  duplicates

## URLs
English pages use English slugs (/en/food/cape-gooseberry). Chinese pages use
Chinese slugs, percent-encoded (/zh/food/%E7%87%88%E7%B1%A0%E6%9E%9C for
燈籠果). An English slug under /zh permanently redirects to the Chinese one, so
either form resolves.

## Citation
Cite as "Food Storage Guide" with a link to the specific page. The underlying
USDA FoodKeeper data is public domain; the written explanations, guides,
research into foods the dataset omits, and the corrections log are original
work.
